liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Feel Like A Stranger** (2 reviews): Reviewer says the jam settled into a nice groove; Reviewer names it the best song of the night [7][16]
- **El Paso** (2 other sources): Source marks El Paso with an asterisk in the setlist; Bob Weir played acoustic guitar on this song [1][4]
- **Sugaree** (1 review): Reviewer calls it one of the best of the tour [12]
- **Corrina** (1 review): Reviewer heard a rocking version with what sounded like a Matilda jam [12]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Reviewer is moved by Jerry's wailing vocal and playing in this version [7]
- **Johnny B. Goode** (1 review): Reviewer found the encore a letdown [9]

## Setlist highlights

- **Pierre Robert Unveils 50th show banner**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1994-10-07.schoeps.wklitz-jones.101803.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 18 songs; 170 min [1]
- **gd94-10-07.aud.wiley.7993.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 17 songs; 168 min; rated 3.5/5 by 6 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the audience recording captures the moment well [7]
- **gd1994-10-07.aud.bleich-sirmick.79019.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 17 songs; 164 min; rated 3.14/5 by 7 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the sound was good; Notes distortion during the loudest part of Drums; polished with iZotope Ozone and light noise reduction [4][13]
- **gd1994-10-07.fob.schoeps.byron.dauria.97255.flac16**: source not stated; 17 songs; 161 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [5]. Said about its sound: Uploader admits the transfer was not done well, with a couple of tracks starting late [5]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says it was the band's 50th Spectrum show, with a tie-dye banner unveiled that night [9]
- Reviewer notes the Spectrum, nicknamed for its poor hockey-rink acoustics, was being demolished in October 2009 [11]
- Reviewer sat second row; local DJ Pierre Robert introduced the concert [12]
- Reviewer arrived after the banner opening; says Jerry wore shorts and the energy was electric [13]
- Reviewer says a local radio host announced the band, and felt Garcia seemed unengaged [14]
- Reviewer says this was one of three consecutive awesome shows, the last of that run [8]
- Reviewer found the setlist ordinary compared with other well-played Spectrum shows, hoping for something special [9]
- Reviewer says both circulating sources are excellent, but this one stands out for clarity [10]
- Reviewer calls the first set okay but the second among the worst ever, blaming Jerry's health and drug problems [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1994-10-07.schoeps.wklitz-jones.101803.flac16**: taped by Keith Litzenberger and Roger Jones; transferred by Keith Litzenberger; source: Schoeps MK4's>Rbox>Sony TCD-D10PROII; from Section 104 Row 5 [1]
- **gd94-10-07.aud.wiley.7993.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Marc P. and Tim W.; source: Audience: Unknown Mics [3]
- **gd1994-10-07.aud.bleich-sirmick.79019.sbeok.flac16**: taped by John Bleich (row 1 seat 21  Section 107); transferred by SirMick and Mark Horvath; source: aud > sony wmd-6 with nak 300 shotguns > mc > wav > cdr > eac > wav > flac [4]. Also: Discs came from John Bleich; discs 2 and 3 are joined seamlessly [4]
- **gd1994-10-07.fob.schoeps.byron.dauria.97255.flac16**: taped by Eliot Byron in the hat on Bill R.; transferred by Frank D'Auria; source: Schoeps CMC5/MK4->Sony D10 F.O.B. D.F.C [5]. Also: Transfer from a Schoeps FOB recording, tracked on the fly with a standalone burner using EAC [5]
